extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO; respondents in USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal proceedings; OED staff and legal regulators
extracted.subtask_description: A final USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline order imposing reciprocal discipline (exclusion from practice before the USPTO in non-patent matters) pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on a state bar disbarment, including restitution, publication, notification, and administrative steps. The page sets out the grounds, statutory/regulatory bases, required remedies, and procedural timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED may impose reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by a state authority (here, disbarment by the Supreme Court of California) pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Notice and Order is issued, the respondent is given an opportunity to respond and oppose within the statutory period (see 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)). If no genuine issue of material fact is shown, reciprocal discipline identical to the state order may be imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/regulatory authority for discipline (35 U.S.C. § 32; 37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions are taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 as the legal basis for imposing discipline on individuals authorized to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutes/regulations authorize OED to impose discipline (including reciprocal discipline) and to follow the procedures set out in the cited regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicate violation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) (discipline predicated upon being disbarred by a duly constituted authority of a State) is a ground for exclusion from practice before the USPTO in non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state disbarment can serve as the predicate for USPTO reciprocal disciplinary action under § 11.804(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and response timeframe (40 days to oppose)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice and Order is to be served (certified mail in this case) and the respondent is provided 40 days to file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery date starts the response period; failure to respond within the timeframe may result in a finding of no genuine issue of material fact and imposition of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard when respondent fails to respond (no genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response, the OED may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and conclude that exclusion is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to contest the complaint supports entry of reciprocal discipline identical to the state order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of exclusion from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is excluded from the practice of trademark and other non-patent matters before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order specifies exclusion scope (trademark/non-patent matters). The document also states the respondent is not authorized to practice before the USPTO in patent matters (indicating overall non-authorization for patent practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restitution requirement (per Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 6140.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall make restitution to identified payees (or other recipients designated by Office of Probation or State Bar Court) or reimburse the Client Security Fund to the extent of any payment from the Fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order specifies amounts and interest for three named payees (Dana & Miguel Lozano: $1,300 plus 10% interest from March 8, 2018; Susan Harper: $1,500 plus 10% interest from October 1, 2017; Mario Curti: $512,000 plus 10% interest from June 29, 2020). Restitution is to be made in accordance with applicable California law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic publication of Final Order (OED FOIA Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in OED's FOIA Reading Room (publicly accessible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions are made publicly available online at the specified FOIA repository URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in the Official Gazette (notice content consistency)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the text provided in the order (summary of exclusion, grounds, and restitution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order includes model language for the Official Gazette notice describing the exclusion, factual bases, and statutory violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED shall give notice of the public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures communication of USPTO discipline to other jurisdictions and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent duties under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order directs compliance but does not recite § 11.58's specific duties on the face of the order; those duties govern obligations such as notification and status reporting following discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from Customer Numbers and USPTO electronic accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate respondent's name from any Customer Number(s) and USPTO-verified Electronic System account(s), if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative steps to prevent the disciplined individual from practicing/filing under existing USPTO electronic credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of misconduct found supporting disbarment
rubrics_metrics.description: The disbarment was based on ethical violations in seven client matters where respondent: failed to perform hired legal services, created and forwarded fabricated documents, provided false information to clients, and failed to return unearned fees upon termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order summarizes concrete misconduct examples that supported the state disbarment and the USPTO reciprocal action.

rubrics_metrics.name: California Business and Professions Code § 6106 (moral turpitude)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation found: intentionally committing an act involving moral turpitude (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 6106).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts involving moral turpitude are ground for state disbarment and thus can predicate USPTO reciprocal discipline under the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: California Business and Professions Code § 6068(iii) (client communication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation found: failing to keep a client reasonably informed of significant developments in a matter in which the attorney agreed to provide legal services (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 6068(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to keep clients reasonably informed is an ethical violation supporting discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: California Business and Professions Code § 6103 (disobeying a court order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation found: disobeying or violating a court order (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 6103).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disobeying court orders is professional misconduct subject to discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: California Business and Professions Code § 6068(i) (failing to cooperate in disciplinary investigation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation found: willfully failing to cooperate and participate in a disciplinary investigation (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 6068(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-cooperation in disciplinary investigations aggravates disciplinary outcomes and supports reciprocal action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Former Rules of Professional Conduct, rule 3-110(A) (competence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation found: intentionally failing to perform legal services with competence (former Rule 3-110(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of competence in performing legal services is a basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Former Rules of Professional Conduct, rule 3-700(D)(2) (return of advanced fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation found: failing to return an advanced fee upon termination of employment (former Rule 3-700(D)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to return advanced/unearned fees after termination is professional misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of Professional Conduct, rule 1.16(e)(2) (return of unearned advanced fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation found: failing to return an unearned advanced fee upon termination of employment (Rule 1.16(e)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attorneys must return unearned fees upon termination; violation supports discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of Professional Conduct, rule 1.15(d)(4) (accounting for funds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation found: failing to promptly account in writing to a client or other person for whom the attorney held funds or property (Rule 1.15(d)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper handling and accounting of client funds is a core ethical requirement; failure to do so is discipline-worthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of Professional Conduct, rule 1.1 (competence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation found: failing to perform services with competence (Rule 1.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competent performance of legal services is required; violations lead to disciplinary measures.
